title: October 2026 Price Cap: What’s Changed and Why
description: The energy price cap rose 4% to £1,723 on 1 October 2026. Here are the new rates, why gas prices rose, how the VAT cut changes things and what to do now.
h1: October 2026 price cap: what’s changed and why
intro: From today, the typical household bill under the cap is £1,723 a year. Gas is up; electricity is broadly flat thanks to a VAT cut.

image.alt: A close-up of a blue gas flame on a hob

cardText: New rates, the gas price rise and what to do now.

sources.title: Ofgem: energy price cap will rise by 4% from October 2026
Ofgem: price cap unit rates and standing charges

sections.html: Ofgem’s cap for 1 October to 31 December 2026 is equivalent to £1,723 a year for a typical dual fuel household on Direct Debit, up £60 (about £5 a month) from £1,663. Average rates: electricity 26.32p/kWh and 54.83p a day; gas 7.97p/kWh and 29.68p a day. Full details in our price cap guide.

Ofgem says higher wholesale gas prices, linked to the conflict in the Middle East, are the main driver, with wholesale costs up about 11% over its assessment window. Gas bills rise around 8%. Electricity is broadly stable because the government has removed VAT from household electricity until 31 March 2027.

• Compare fixed deals: Ofgem says some are £100 or more below the cap. See how to compare deals.
  • Check you’re on the cheapest payment method: prepay and Direct Debit beat paying on receipt of a bill.
  • If you’re struggling, contact your supplier now and check grants and support.
